name: Raymond Castellano
presenting_complaint: Sudden right-sided weakness and slurred speech

medical_history.social: Ex-smoker. Lives with wife, independent with all ADLs at baseline.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 72-year-old man is brought in by ambulance as a Code Stroke. His wife noticed sudden right facial droop, right arm weakness and slurred speech. He was last seen well 50 minutes ago. He takes apixaban for atrial fibrillation. BP 184/102, GCS 14. This is an acute stroke presentation within the reperfusion window.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: Establish and document the TIME LAST KNOWN WELL — not the time the patient was found
FAST/deficit description: facial droop, arm weakness, speech disturbance, onset circumstances
Thrombolysis checklist history: anticoagulant use (apixaban), recent surgery/bleeding, prior ICH, recent stroke
Collateral history from wife/ambulance; premorbid functional status (modified Rankin)
State: low glucose is the great stroke mimic, so it must be checked first
objective: Check the blood glucose (BGL) immediately — exclude hypoglycaemia as a mimic
Urgent non-contrast CT brain plus CT angiography per Code Stroke protocol
Obs, IV access, ECG (looking for AF), bloods including coagulation profile
Swallow screen before any oral intake
assessment: Acute ischaemic stroke (likely cardioembolic given AF) — confirm on imaging
Must exclude intracranial haemorrhage on CT before any antithrombotic
Consider stroke mimics: hypoglycaemia, seizure/Todd's paresis, migraine, sepsis
plan: Establish time last known well, THEN check blood glucose (FIRST actions)
Activate the local Code Stroke pathway; notify stroke team
Obs, IV access, bloods including coags, ECG, urgent non-contrast CT + CTA per protocol
Assess NIHSS, premorbid function, anticoagulant use, recent surgery/bleeding (thrombolysis checklist)
Do NOT give aspirin until haemorrhage is excluded on CT; note apixaban is a relative contraindication to thrombolysis
Permissive hypertension: do NOT lower BP aggressively; only treat if above thrombolysis threshold (approx >185/110) and then cautiously per protocol
Nil by mouth until a formal swallow screen is done
Stroke team to decide thrombolysis vs endovascular clot retrieval; consider retrieval/transfer if large-vessel occlusion

critical_errors: Dropping the blood pressure aggressively in acute ischaemic stroke (worsens penumbral perfusion)
Giving aspirin or other antithrombotic before intracranial haemorrhage is excluded on CT
Failing to document time last known well and/or failing to check blood glucose
must_not_miss: Time last known well established and documented
Hypoglycaemia excluded as a stroke mimic (BGL checked)
Intracranial haemorrhage excluded on CT before antithrombotics; large-vessel occlusion considered for clot retrieval
